definition: For q=lambda*onehot(y_a)+(1-lambda)*onehot(y_b), CE(q,p)=H(q)+KL(q||p); H(q)=binary_entropy(lambda) for different classes, otherwise zero. Epoch values weight each batch by its actual sample count.
weighted_accuracy_upper_bound_definition: Mean max_c q_c: 1 for same-class pairs, max(lambda,1-lambda) otherwise. This is a target-based ceiling, not ordinary hard-label accuracy.

replay.source: E3 initial.pt NumPy and train loader RNG states; labels only from manifest train indices
replay.dataset_access_note: CIFAR-10 training loader was used to obtain labels; only the training-index labels entered replay, with no image transforms or model forward.

notes: Entropy and excess KL are in natural-log units (nats); targets come from the exact replayed same-class/different-class pairing, not an assumed class-match probability.

Training objective was recorded under AMP with train-mode BN/Dropout. CE=H+KL is the mathematical decomposition; subtracting exact H from recorded CE gives a numerical diagnostic up to floating-point effects.
High correlation over late epochs describes observed variation; it is not a separate causal experiment or a guarantee that longer training cannot help.
The positive entropy floor explains why mixed-label CE should not be expected to approach zero; the positive excess KL means the entire remaining loss cannot be called unavoidable target entropy.
Late objective/entropy correlation does not mean all fluctuations are unavoidable entropy: excess KL also varies with mixture difficulty; only H(q) is the explicit target-entropy floor.
